does: Stirs miso smooth into a little warm liquid away from the main pot, and then stirs it into the pot at the end, so that it never clumps and its scent is not boiled away.

intro.what: Miso is loosened in warm liquid and blended into soup near the end without boiling it again.
intro.why: Working the paste smooth prevents hidden lumps, while gentle finishing preserves the aroma that miso brings to the soup.

how: Heat the soup or stock and turn off the heat or lower it until the liquid only trembles.
Put the miso in a ladle or a small sieve and lower it into the liquid.
Work the miso loose with the back of a spoon or a whisk until it has all gone into the liquid.
Stir the pot once, taste, and serve before it cools. Never let it come back to a boil.

cues.text: The soup turns evenly cloudy and there are no lumps.
The miso scent is full and warm, and is not flat.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the miso into the pot in a lump, so that it sinks and stays in clots.
mistakes.fix: Dissolve it in a ladle of warm liquid first.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling the soup after the miso is in, which dulls its scent.
mistakes.fix: Take it off the heat first and serve right away.

quiz.question: Why dissolve miso separately rather than dropping in a lump?
choices: To keep its flavour separate from the broth until serving.
To make the paste settle rather than cloud the soup.
To distribute it without clots of paste.
quiz.because: Loosening the paste first helps it disperse evenly through the soup.

quiz.question: How should the main pot be heated when miso is added?
choices: Off the heat or lowered until the liquid only trembles.
Boiled harder after the paste enters.
quiz.because: The method uses gentle finishing to avoid dulling the miso aroma.

quiz.question: Which appearance suggests the paste has dispersed?
choices: Dense paste clots below clear liquid.
Dry crumbs floating above an unchanged broth.
quiz.because: A uniformly cloudy soup shows that the miso has been worked into the liquid.

quiz.question: The soup contains sunken clumps of miso. What should change?
choices: Boil the clumps harder without working them.
Loosen the paste in warm liquid before blending it in.
quiz.because: Working the paste smooth addresses the clumps instead of relying on harsh boiling.
